note: Pre-registered parameters for the disclosed self-trading experiment. AMENDED TWICE on 19 Aug 2026 and a third time on 20 Aug. First, after five trades: a single pivot made every trade near it flip direction, so the wallet alternated buy/sell/buy/sell like a metronome. Replaced with a band — buy while the USDC balance falls, sell while it rises, reverse only at 10 and 20 — which produces runs of one to three trades in the same direction. seed_usdc was removed in the same amendment: it governed nothing in the worker and named a figure the wallets were never funded to. The band is self-funding — below the lower bound an arm sells tokens for USDC, above the upper it buys — so no arm ever needs topping up, and the only consumable is gas. Both changes are recorded as events in the log and the rules hash moved with them, which is what the hash is for. This file is committed BEFORE the first trade; its canonical hash is written into the market D1 rules row, and the worker refuses to trade unless its bundled copy hashes to the same value. Changing anything here is a visible commit that the running worker will reject until the row is updated on purpose. See docs/drafts/wash-worker-blueprint.md and the diary entry that names this what it is: wash trading, disclosed. THIRD AMENDMENT, 20 Aug 2026, after the BYKO arm halted on its own price-deviation guard at 64.1%: all eight of its trades had been buys and not one a sell. The wallet was funded to $34.32 while its band tops out at $20, and the rule 'buy while the balance is above the upper bound' then obliged it to spend $24 in one direction before it could ever reverse. Twenty-four dollars into a pool holding $123 is a 64% price move, so the guard was tripped by the strategy's own design rather than by anything going wrong. Two parameters are added and the guard itself is NOT touched: it fired correctly, and widening a limit because it caught something is the exact move this project exists to criticise. run_reverse_pct makes a run reverse once the pool price has moved that far from where the run began, so the excursion is bounded by price rather than by how much cash happens to sit in the wallet. max_trade_pct_pool clamps the drawn size to a share of the pool's USDC reserve: $9 was 6% of this pool and moved the price ~12% in a single trade, which would spend a whole run in one step, while the same $9 in a deep pool would be nothing. An instrument has to scale to what it measures. FOURTH AMENDMENT, 20 Aug 2026, within the hour, after the byko arm was resumed and halted again 31 seconds later on the same 64.1%. Three changes. (1) A fixed run_reverse_pct is itself a pattern: every run would turn at exactly +15% and −15%, which draws a metronome on the chart just as the single pivot did, only slower. It becomes a RANGE, drawn once per run and recorded in wallet_state.run_target_pct before the run starts, so the figure is committed in advance and published rather than chosen after the fact. (2) The band and the percentage are now ordered as a constraint over a trigger: the drawn percentage decides when a run turns, and the band overrides it whenever the balance would leave 10–20. Previously the percentage could override the band, which is the wrong way round — the band is the outer limit, not a suggestion. (3) max_price_deviation_pct becomes DIRECTIONAL, and this is the change that needs the most scrutiny. Its value is untouched at 60 and 80. What changes is that beyond the limit the arm may still make a trade that moves the price back toward the start price, and still may not make one that moves it further away. As written before, an arm that reached the limit could never trade again in any direction, so the inflated price it had created was frozen there permanently — the guard prevented the recovery as firmly as it prevented the abuse. A limit that forbids unwinding what it just caught is not a stricter limit, it is a broken one. FIFTH AMENDMENT, 23 Aug 2026, after 124 confirmed trades: 77 of them (62%) had landed on the pool cap to the cent — 3.61, 3.57, 3.49 in a row in a log that called itself random. The cause was the order of two honest operations: the size was drawn uniformly from trade_usdc [0.30, 9.00] and THEN clamped to max_trade_pct_pool, and with the pool near $144 the cap sat at ~$3.60, so 62% of the uniform mass collapsed onto a single point — exactly the share the arithmetic predicts, (9.00−3.60)/8.70. No parameter changes. What changes is that the draw now happens over the effective range [trade_usdc min, min(trade_usdc max, cap)] — the same range the page has published as 'drawn from' all along — so the published claim and the distribution finally say the same thing. The clamp itself stays, with the last word, for the corner where the pool shrinks below the minimum between the read and the trade. Consequences worth stating out loud: the average trade gets smaller (the mean of the effective range is ~$1.95, not ~$3.58 as the pile-up produced) and small sizes stop being rare, which is the spread the log was supposed to show from the start. SIXTH AMENDMENT, 23 Aug 2026, and this one changes parameters, so it gets the scrutiny clause up front: the fifth amendment fixed the sizes and left the rhythm, and the rhythm was the tell. With every trade near the cap and the reversal target drawn from 5-15%, a run spent itself in two or three trades; the $10 band corridor enforced the same count from the cash side; and a pure run process cannot print a lone contrarian trade at all, because direction only changes at a reversal. The ledger read b-b-b s-s-s b-b-b — a metronome with a three-count, which is the pattern the second amendment was supposed to bury. Three changes, together: run_reverse_pct widens from [5,15] to [3,35], so a run can be a twitch or an excursion; band_usdc widens from [10,20] to [10,30], because a corridor of five mean-sized trades caps every run at five whatever the price target says — the corridor is now ~$20 and the self-funding property is untouched, no wallet is topped up; and contrarian_pct is new at 20: one fire in five trades against its own run, drawn by the same CSPRNG as every other figure at the moment of the fire, from a probability published here in advance — the same pre-registration every other drawn figure gets, a published distribution with no discretion in the draw. The noise is subordinate to everything: it fires only inside the band (outside it the corrective side is forced, and noise would un-force it), only within the deviation guard's limit, only when the opposite leg can fund the trade, and it does not touch the run's direction, clock or target — a contrarian trade is a trade against the run, not a shorter run. Every contrarian trade names itself in the public events log, so nobody has to take the coin's word for it. Stated plainly, because this project does not get to pretend otherwise: the purpose of these three changes is to make manufactured flow look less manufactured. That is what wash trading is for, it is what this experiment exists to demonstrate in the open, and a demonstration that fools nobody demonstrates nothing. SEVENTH AMENDMENT, 26 Aug 2026: the wait between trades is drawn log-uniformly from the same 5-180 minute bounds. The linear draw weighted minutes, not scales: a gap of 5-10 minutes had a 2.9% chance while 150-180 had 17%, so nearly every pause came out at an hour or more and the stream read as a steady beat around ninety minutes - the ledger's measured mean was 96.7 and 96.9 minutes per arm, faithful to the rule and monotonous to the eye. Log-uniform gives every doubling of the wait the same probability, about 19% per octave across 5-10, 10-20, 20-40, 40-80 and 80-160 minutes, so five-minute bursts, half-hour pauses and three-hour silences now arrive mixed and unpredictable. The bounds are untouched; the next fire time is still drawn in advance, written into the trade row, and published on the page before it happens. Consequences stated in advance: the median gap falls from 92 to 30 minutes and the mean to about 49, so each arm trades roughly twice as often; gas burn doubles, which on Base is cents; and at current sizes each arm's 600-dollar gross-spend cap is reached in roughly half the calendar time it would otherwise have taken. Same honesty clause as the sixth: a more lifelike pulse makes manufactured flow harder to spot, that is the whole point of wash trading, and this file says so in public before the first draw. EIGHTH AMENDMENT, 28 Aug 2026: the reserve-jump skip is removed and max_reserve_jump_pct (both arms at 25) is deleted. The rule compared the pool's USDC reserve against its level after the arm's own last trade and skipped the fire on a move past 25% — 'not trading into an unknown move'. The flaw is a deadlock: the baseline it compares against only advances when the arm actually trades, so any large legitimate change locks the arm out for good. On 27 Aug a real buyer (the wallet the register calls BYKO Anon) took 144,652 BYKO out of the pool in one purchase — the experiment working exactly as intended, an outside party buying — which moved the USDC reserve 57.1% from where byko's last trade left it. From then on every byko fire read a 57.1% jump and skipped; it could not trade, so the baseline never caught up, so the jump never fell back under 25%: the arm was frozen with no way out. A guard that cannot tell a genuine buy from manipulation, and then permanently stops the instrument on the former, protects nothing and defeats the experiment. It is removed rather than widened, because widening it would still deadlock at the higher number; the per-trade price-deviation guard (60/80%, directional since the fourth amendment) still bounds how far any single trade may move the price, which is the protection that actually matters.
